name: Terror of the Peaks
oracle_text:
Flying
Spells your opponents cast that target this creature cost an additional 3 life to cast.
Whenever another creature you control enters, this creature deals damage equal to that creature's power to any target.
blocked_sentences: Spells your opponents cast that target this creature cost an additional 3 life to cast.

needs.what: A static that RAISES the price of somebody else's spell, and can charge that raise in life rather than mana. The natural spelling is the mirror of `spell_cost_reduction` (src/automtg/engine/player_statics.py:622), which already has every other piece this line needs: `affects_spells: {"controller": "opponent"}` says whose spells (SPELL_FILTER_KEYS carries `controller`, vocabulary.py:552), and `targeting: {"self_only": true}` says "that target this creature" -- that clause exists and is read against the refs the cast chose (Strong Back, "Aura spells you cast that target enchanted creature", player_statics.py:642-648). What does not exist is the direction and the resource. Two ways to add it, both small: (a) a new `spell_cost_tax` static effect whose `cost` is a whole cost node from `cost_keys` (as `ward` and `attack_tax` already take one, loader/__init__.py:2760-2795), added to `static_effects` in vocabulary.py, summed in a new `player_statics.spell_cost_tax` beside `spell_cost_reduction`, and folded into the cast path in `casting.py` (the point near line 1179 where the reduction statics are already gathered) so that the extra cost is both offered by legality and charged by payment through the one helper -- `costs.life_cost` (costs.py:816) already prices a life payment and `casting.py:808` already charges one, but only for a cost node the CASTER's own card printed; or (b) the narrower `spell_life_tax` that carries just an integer, if a general cost node on somebody else's spell is more than the engine wants. Either way the caster must be able to decline (they simply do not cast), and the life must be paid as part of casting, not as a resolution effect.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `spell_cost_reduction` is the closest thing and points the wrong way twice. Its loader branch (loader/__init__.py:2338-2361) demands an `amount` and documents it as a reduction; `cost_reduction.reduction_amount` (cost_reduction.py:46) is subtracted and clamped, and `costs.cost_reduction` clamps at zero, so even a negative `amount` cannot become a surcharge -- it would round away to "costs nothing extra" and load clean, which is the silent-wrong-card failure the brief forbids. And it is mana arithmetic end to end: schema.py:513-516 says so outright -- "that one lowers a mana cost by an amount and cannot swap the payment to a different resource entirely" -- so it could never charge 3 LIFE. `ward` is the other near miss and is a materially different card. It is a triggered ability that counters the spell unless its controller pays (characteristics.py:1665, `granted_wards`), so: it fires on ABILITIES as well as spells, where Terror of the Peaks taxes spells only; it resolves after the spell is already cast and on the stack rather than pricing it at cast time; the opponent chooses whether to pay AFTER committing their spell, and declining costs them the spell instead of merely costing them life; and a countered ward'd spell never resolves, where a paid-for Terror tax always does. Writing the line as ward would hand the Dragon a much stronger and differently-shaped protection than is printed. `attack_tax` is a tax but only over the declare-attackers step, and the loader explicitly refuses it anything but mana (loader/__init__.py:2771-2790, "attack_tax is paid in mana; give its 'cost' a 'mana'"). The card-level `additional_cost` / `additional_cost_options` (schema.py:888, 904) are the right *price* -- a cost node that can hold `pay_life` -- but the wrong direction of ownership: they are fields on the card being cast, charging its own caster, and nothing lets a permanent on the battlefield hang one onto an opponent's spell. `becomes_target` is a trigger, not a cost, and cannot stop or price a cast; making the opponent lose 3 life after the fact is a different card (it would still apply if the spell were countered, and it could not be declined by not paying). No `cost_increase`, `spell_tax` or `spell_cost_increase` string exists anywhere in the engine today.

notes: Only the second printed line is blocked -- the other two are expressible today and should not be re-explored when this gap is closed. Flying is a keyword already in the packet's starting_point. The third line is an ordinary triggered ability: trigger `{"event": "permanent_enters", "controller": "you", "filter": {"types": ["Creature"], "controller": "you", "exclude_self": true}}` with a `damage` op whose `amount` is `{"power_of": {"binding": "<the entering creature>"}}` and a single target of `kind: "any"` with NO selector -- "any target" is a creature, player or planeswalker, and narrowing it with `selector: {"types": ["Creature"]}` (as a sibling card in this deck was mistakenly authored) makes a strictly worse card. When the tax is built, the whole card should be one answer; note that the sandbox expectation for it would fall back to `{"zone": "battlefield"}` plus `battlefield_count: 33`, because nothing in the fixed position makes another creature enter after the Dragon resolves, so the enters trigger never fires and its damage cannot be asserted.
